title: Actions against Publication of Fake News
what_it_is: Actions against Publication of Fake News

sections.label: Fake news laws and penalties
sections.summary: Questions asked the Minister for Law about strengthening penalties, setting up an agency, correcting false information and foreign manipulation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Law whether the existing laws can be strengthened to increase the penalties against the author or publisher of fake news on the Internet.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
sentences.text: asked	the Minister for Law (a) whether the Ministry will consider setting up an agency to look into the proliferation of fake news on the Internet; (b) what are the Ministry's plans to correct false information in a timely manner; and (c) what is the Ministry's assessment on the likelihood that such news can be manipulated by foreign parties to influence society, including election outcomes and social cohesion.

sections.label: Germany draft fake news fines
sections.summary: Germany is suggesting fines of up to €50 million under draft legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In Germany, it is being suggested that they will face fines of up to €50 million, which is a lot of money, under the draft legislation.

sections.label: The Real Singapore false articles
sections.summary: The Real Singapore earned over $500,000 from false articles; a former editor registered States Times Review, which publishes fake news from outside Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: One of the editors was also charged for writing another false article, on puppy mills, which she passed off as being written by a Malay Singaporean. "The Real Singapore" owners made more than $500,000 in advertising revenues by publishing these completely false articles.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Evidence showed that the couple had paid off most of their A$190,000 (S$191,768) 30-year home loan in just 11 months.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: So, it is very attractive. "The Real Singapore" has ceased operations, but one of its former editors and co-founder, Alex Tan Zhixiang, has since registered another website called the "States Times Review" which continues to publish completely false, fake news from outside Singapore.

sections.label: All Singapore Stuff Fernandez letter
sections.summary: In November last year, All Singapore Stuff published a letter attributed to someone called Fernandez about citizenship.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: In November last year, "All Singapore Stuff" published a letter supposed to have been written by someone called "Fernandez" with the headline, "Singapore new citizen feels cheated, now wants his old citizenship back".

sections.label: Punggol Waterway Terraces collapse article
sections.summary: In November 2016, All Singapore Stuff said the rooftop of Punggol Waterway Terraces had collapsed.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: Another article, again in November 2016 last year, again in "All Singapore Stuff", said the rooftop of Punggol Waterway Terraces had collapsed.

sections.label: Government considering fake news issue
sections.summary: The Government is seriously considering how to address the fake news issue.

sentences.speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
sentences.text: The Government is seriously considering how to address this fake news issue.
